label: Photo Explainer
tagline: Real, specific things shown as full-frame pictures: products, screens, named people and places.

picture.opening: Scene 1 shows the subject of the first sentence from frame 0, already moving: a photograph already pushing in. Never a title card, a blank or black frame, or an abstract gradient.
picture.turn: A new scene starts on the first word of a turn or a re-opening, and its picture is visibly different from the scene before (a new image, a new place, a tighter crop of the real thing). Never merge that segment into the scene before it.
picture.payoff: The payoff scene gets the video's strongest picture: the hero image of the real thing, full frame.
picture.ending: Hold on the payoff picture to the last frame. No closing card, logo, recap or sign-off after it.

best_for: real, specific things the viewer came to see as full-frame pictures: products, buildings, artworks, machines, named people and places
a real event, accident or failure and its cause, shown with the real machine, place or company; a diagram of the cause becomes a System Flow insert
avoid_for: topics whose beats are generic roles acted out by people
a mechanism, process or flow that diagrams carry (a richer style carries it, with System Flow inserts)
an abstract idea with nothing real to photograph
routing.cannot_show: drawn figures acting out a step: it draws no figures, and people appear only in photographs
signals: the script names specific real things that are best shown as pictures
most beats want a full-frame photograph of a real thing, none wants a character
a real, dated event happens to a named machine, company or place
